# Dire Wolf (AX.25 packet TNC) — bundled as a separate executable

[Dire Wolf](https://github.com/wb2osz/direwolf) by John Langner (WB2OSZ) is
the software TNC POTACAT uses for Winlink packet (AX.25) on VHF/UHF. POTACAT
launches it only for a packet session and Pat talks to it over its loopback
AGWPE port — never linked (the wsprd posture).

- License: GNU GPL v2 (`LICENSE`, copied from the pinned tag)
- Pinned: see `VERSION.txt`
- Built by `scripts/build-winlink-helpers.sh` **with Hamlib** (the build fails
  otherwise): Windows links the official hamlib-w64-4.7.0 zip (checksum-pinned),
  Linux links `libhamlib-dev` and ships the `.so` beside it (RPATH `$ORIGIN`),
  macOS links Homebrew's Hamlib (plus the PortAudio and hidapi its CMake
  requires there) and ships the `.dylib`s beside it (`bundle-mac-deps.js`,
  `@loader_path`, architecture-checked). Staged to `assets/direwolf/`, packaged
  to `resources/direwolf/`.
- **Its only PTT is `PTT RIG 2 127.0.0.1:<shim>`** — Hamlib's NET rig client
  pointed at POTACAT's loopback rigctld shim, so POTACAT keys the radio
  (`lib/direwolf-process.js`). No beacons, digipeating, IGate or KISS port.
- **Socket audio backend** (`src/audio_tcp.c` + `src/audio_tcp.h`, hooked
  into `audio.c` / `audio_win.c` / `audio_portaudio.c`, `audio.h` and the
  CMake source list by `potacat-socket-audio.patch`, generated by
  `scripts/gen-direwolf-patch.py` from the pinned sources): `ADEVICE
  tcp:<port>` makes Dire Wolf take its receive audio from, and send its
  transmit audio to, the loopback port POTACAT serves (16-bit mono at the
  configured `ARATE`, 48 kHz, raw, both ways) — it opens no sound device on
  any OS. POTACAT carries that audio to the radio the way it does for FT8
  (Flex Direct, Icom Network, or the modem bridge window on a sound-card
  rig), so nothing is picked and no DAX program or virtual cable is needed.
  The backend paces transmit audio like a sound card with a small buffer and
  `audio_wait()` sleeps until the last sample has played, so Dire Wolf drops
  PTT no earlier than it would with real hardware. GPL-2: a patch to a
  separately built, separately run program; the patch and the source ship
  here with the pointer to the pinned tag, as the ardopcf one does.
- Regenerating the patch when the pin moves: fetch `src/audio.c`,
  `audio_win.c`, `audio_portaudio.c`, `audio.h` and `src/CMakeLists.txt` from
  the new tag into one folder and run
  `python scripts/gen-direwolf-patch.py <folder> third_party/direwolf/potacat-socket-audio.patch`;
  every anchor asserts it occurs exactly once.
